page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-384-metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Providing bare-metal access to dedicated compute hardware, it is equipped with 384 dedicated vCPUs and 1536 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This hardware profile provides extensive parallel execution resources and substantial memory bandwidth without hypervisor virtualization overhead.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, having zero GPUs bundled. Storage requirements must be satisfied via attached network-based block volumes. Network configuration also excludes complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating private networking or dedicated address allocation for external routing.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the c4d-standard-384-metal consolidates heavy enterprise compute requirements onto a single non-virtualized physical machine. This design eliminates virtualization jitter, making it appropriate for massive multi-threaded applications, large memory-resident enterprise databases, high-throughput batch data processing, and large container orchestration hosts.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-384-metal is an x86_64 bare-metal general-purpose server configured with 384 dedicated vCPUs and 1536 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Operating directly on dedicated hardware without virtualization overhead, the instance provides raw access to substantial processing density and memory capacity. It includes zero bundled GPUs and has no local ephemeral NVMe storage, meaning all persistence relies on remote block storage solutions. The system also omits complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Delivering extensive parallel core count and massive unified memory on physical silicon, the c4d-standard-384-metal is well suited for demanding multi-threaded enterprise workloads, high-concurrency transactional databases, extensive in-memory analytics, and container consolidation platforms.
